title: Inference Flow Notebook: chaining, fallbacks, and dev UX
content:
Goal / motivation:
- Too many product features at Redwood require composing multiple LLM calls (prompt -> reranker -> extract -> tool call). Building these ad-hoc leads to duplicated retry logic, poor observability, and unclear cost attribution.
- Idea: lightweight developer-first "flow" abstraction + console playground + local simulator so engineers can prototype, debug, and ship composed inference pipelines with standard SLOs and fallback semantics.

Key problems to solve (user POV):
- How do I express dependent calls with branching and fallbacks without reinventing orchestration each time?
- How do I test locally with representative latency/cost without hitting prod models?
- How can Product and SRE see per-flow token cost and failure hotspots?
- How to define safe defaults for retries, timeouts, and degrade-to-cheaper model?

High-level feature sketch (rough primitives)
- Flow manifest (yaml/json): nodes (call, transform, condition, tool), edges, k/v context. Example: call(gpt-4o) -> condition(score>0.8) -> call(embedding) else -> call(gpt-3-mini) -> tool(call-api)
- Node-level policies: timeout, max_retries, retry_backoff, fallback_model, cost_budget, required_confidence
- Observability hooks: per-node latency/cost, token breakdown, traces that map back to flow manifest
- Dev playground: replay a conversation, step debugger (inspect context), simulate slow GPU result, toggle deterministic RNG, stubbed tool outputs
- Local simulator: run flows with local stubbed models or smaller quantized variants, ingest sample telemetry to preview SLO effects

Success metrics (initial)
- Developer adoption: 12 internal teams try flow playground in first 6 weeks
- Reduction: 30% fewer build-from-scratch orchestration PRs in "solutions-engineering" repo
- Reliability: 25% reduction in production incidents caused by flow misconfiguration (first 3 months)
- Observability: ability to attribute >90% of per-flow cost to nodes in console

User stories (short):
- As a product engineer, I want to define a flow manifest that chains generation -> rerank -> extract so I can focus on prompts not plumbing.
- As an SRE, I want per-node SLIs and automatic fallback to cheaper models so customer-facing pages stay up during load spikes.
- As an ML engineer, I want to run the flow locally against sample inputs and a faster quantized model to speed iteration.
- As a PM, I want a console view that highlights which node in the flow contributes most to cost or flakiness.

API sketches (thinking out loud):
- POST /flows (manifest) -> flow_id
- POST /flows/{flow_id}/run {input, mode:[prod|simulate|local], trace:true} -> run_id
- GET /flows/{flow_id}/runs/{run_id}/trace -> trace payload (tokens, latencies, node statuses)

Console UX notes:
- Flow editor: left pane nodes, middle canvas, right pane properties. Support for import/export to manifest YAML.
- Run playground: choose input, mode, and failure scenarios (slow node, wrong tool output). Step-through execution with context inspector.
- Cost/health dashboard: per-flow trends, hottest nodes (CPU/GPU time + token cost), recent failures with suggested remediations (increase timeout, add fallback).

Rollout plan (MVP phases):
- Phase 0 (internal alpha): CLI + manifest runner + basic trace events. Target: 2 teams, manual onboarding.
- Phase 1 (internal beta): Console playground, local simulator, per-node cost telemetry. Target: 10 teams.
- Phase 2 (external opt-in): Documented API, samples, template flows for typical patterns (QA summarization, search-then-rewrite).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How much complexity do we expose vs hidden defaults? (e.g., advanced retry graphs vs single fallback)
- Execution model: synchronous stepper vs DAG executor with concurrency. Need to support both low-latency linear flows and parallel scoring.
- Security: flows may call customer tools or webhooks. Need safe execution sandbox, secret handling, and audit trail.
- Cost budgeting: should flows support hard spend caps that circuit-break mid-run? What is UX when a run is aborted due to budget?
- Persistence: store full node traces (big) vs sampled traces for long-term retention.

Implementation notes (initial tech ideas):
- Reuse existing runtime routing and cache layers for model calls so flows benefit from batching and KV caching.
- Instrument each model call with a lightweight trace envelope that includes tokens_in/tokens_out, model_id, quantization_flag.
- Local simulator = small binary that can either call local quantized runtime or replay canned traces.

Quick sketch of a manifest example:
```
flow: ticket-qa-summarize
nodes:
  - id: gen
    type: call
    model: gpt-4o-mini
    policies:
      timeout_ms: 2000
      fallback_model: gpt-3-mini
  - id: score
    type: call
    model: reranker-v1
  - id: if_pass
    type: condition
    expr: score.output >= 0.82
  - id: publish
    type: tool
    tool: post-to-cms
edges:
  - from: gen
    to: score
  - from: score
    to: if_pass
  - from: if_pass
    to: publish
```

Next actions (me):
- Draft a short RFC for eng-serving-runtime + devex outlining data model and trace schema (by 2026-03-15).
- Prototype a tiny CLI runner that reads manifest and executes against a stubbed model (PoC due 2026-04-01).
- Schedule 30m sync with Maya + Noah to validate the openness of the manifest design and see overlap with "tooling for rollouts" work.

Notes to self / parking lot ideas:
- Could we allow "composable policies" that are shared across flows (timeout profiles, cost profiles)?
- Explore ability to attach golden prompt sets to flows for continuous quality checks (integrate with Optimize).
- Consider a low-code flow gallery in the console for PMs to compose flows visually.
- Think about per-customer flow templates for Dedicated/Private where model choices are constrained by compliance.
